images.caption: Eilean Chaluim Chille Eilean Chaluim Chille is a small tidal island at the mouth of Loch Èireasort.  It is used nowadays only for grazing sheep, but near its southern shore are the ruins of Eaglais Chaluim Chille (St Columba's Church), which can be seen in the centre of the photo.  It is thought that there has been a church on this site since around 800AD.  The graveyard was used until the second half of the 19th century and some legible stones still remain.

images.filename: South-western corner of Eilean Chaluim Chille - geograph.org.uk - 497465.jpg
images.caption: South-western corner of Eilean Chaluim Chille The extreme north-eastern tip of the grid square is occupied by this corner of Eilean Chaluim Chille, a small island in Loch Èireasort.  This view looks across the loch to the mainland of Lewis near Cabharstadh.  The photo was taken despite the strenuous efforts of a couple of great black-backed gulls to deter the photographer from encroaching on their territory!

images.caption: A dry crossing? Eilean Chaluim Chille can be reached by a causeway at low tide. On this occasion the water was still 15cm deep over the causeway, so the question was whether the tide was falling or rising. If the water is flowing left to right, then the tide is still going out.

images.caption: Eaglais Chaluim Chille The remains of the church of St Columba on the small island that also bears the saint's name. There is little to be seen here except for ruined walls and some grassed over mounds, whilst dating beyond the medieval period is difficult. The site dates back to the 7th century.
